questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The mix of getting to experiencing Australia (a pleace I've always wanted to visit) for a longer period of time, with a university that offers cool and different courses from what I have at home

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Everyone at UTS is super friendly, so you can always ask if you're in doubt. You get all the info you need through email, so it's pretty easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Orientation week with all information you need

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: A dorm with different types of rooms

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Single studio or shared accom. with shared kitchen

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It's very convenient for school, and is located in the cente rof the city, so everything is pretty accessible from there. Most students living there are 18-21 yrs on average, and danes are generally a bit older, so just a matter if that matters to you or not. Everyone is super sweet in general.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You commit to 6 months of housing, when the semester is only 12 weeks. If you find a UTS student to take over the room, you can move out, but not everyone managed to do so. People are generally a bit younger, so not everyone is super cleanly, but really depends on which roommates you get, of course

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Remember to be quick when applying for classes! Its first come first serve

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Any help you could imagine - phone, mail, in person

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got two I had planned to get, and then had to find two others, but one of the extras actually turned out to be my favourite

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try to be on top of deadlines and be prepared to be awake at wierd times of the day when applying for dorms/classes due to time difference

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I was on my fifth semester (BA) and took second and first semester classes at UTS, so the level was definitely lower. It's nice and more industry focused, which I like, and I only had 7 hours of classes a week:)

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Way more industry focused and practical with more writing and producing excersices during classes. Sometimes almost "folkeskole"-ish

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Creative Advertising, Creative non-fiction, News Now and Aboriginal Sydney Now

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I loved Creative non-fiction, since it was a fun and active writing class with cool teacers, while Aboriginal Sydney Now was very interesting and eye-opening

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Groceries are just a little bit more expensive, and you spend more money on experiences (which is all worth it)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Coffee was half price compared to DK:)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Over 100 social and sports clubs, excursions for exchange students

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go on the trips with UTS Activate

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Uluru! 
And rentiing a car going either south to Wollongong or nort to Port Stephens for a weekend

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: super easy, Australians are very easy going

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to join the events at the school, people are very social

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really any

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The easy-goingness and aussie slang

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Remember to talk to other nationalities than danish (we do that too often, and this is a great opportunity to learn a lot from other cultures with fun unexpected stories)
Uni work is generally easier than here, but depends on how much effort you put into it - Choose fun courses, now you have the chance
Get out and see the different beaches and parts of the city!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The semester is only 13 weeks (including a break)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the travelling I got to do and people I got to meet:)

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Settling in and adjusting to being so far away from home and your friends in the first month

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy:)

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
